text:
Julia: Quick heads-up — did a small sweep comparing speculative decoding vs baseline greedy on the new quantized Llama3-13B build. Short summary: ~1.7-1.9x token throughput (p50 latency down), but we see a consistent shift in long-answer factuality metrics on the QA suite.
Kevin: dmg — which QA suite and what metrics?
Julia: ran `eval/qa_suite_v2` (subset 10k), metrics: ExactMatch, F1, and a custom hallucination score. ExactMatch down ~2.1 pts, F1 down ~1.4, hallucination rate up ~1.8%.
Sandra: can you paste the run config? especially the speculative params (spec_ratio / timeout / fallback policy)
Julia: sure —
```
model: llama3-13b-quant
decode: speculative
speculative: {
  spec_ratio: 0.35
  candidate_k: 3
  timeout_ms: 8
  fallback: greedy_if_no_agreement
}
batch_size: 32
sequence_len: 512
```
Julia: also ran with spec_ratio=0.2 and 0.5 for sanity — quality deltas scale with ratio.
Kevin: interesting — did you control for random seed / sampling temperature? speculative can interact badly with temp.
Julia: temp=0.0 for all runs (deterministic within spec algorithm), seeds logged. The model is quantized to 4-bit with per-channel scale.
Sandra: what about prefix length/QA context? long-form answers only?
Julia: split by question length: for short answers (<50 tokens) spec perf is neutral-to-positive; for long answers (>200 tokens) EM drops are more visible. Hypothesis: speculative introduces early commit errors that cascade with longer decode horizons.
Kevin: could be a bias-variance tradeoff — spec reduces per-token variance (faster) but biases toward high-prob prefixes that sometimes omit low-prob but correct continuations.
Sandra: can we run a calibration eval: keep spec_ratio but increase candidate_k to 5 and raise timeout to 12ms to see if we recover EM? also run adversarial QA subset.
Julia: queued a follow-up sweep: spec_ratio:{0.2,0.35,0.5}, candidate_k:{3,5}, timeout_ms:{8,12}, plus baseline greedy and nucleus sampling at T=0.7 as control.
DeployBot: scheduled job 2956789240: `spec_eval_sweep_v1` on dedicated-ml-pool, ETA ~2h.
Kevin: add logging for first-diff token positions and a tiny metric for "early-commit precision" (fraction of times the speculative candidate that wins agreed with greedy top-1 at each commit point).
Julia: good call — I added `early_commit_agreement` to the eval harness.
Sandra: we should also run a human spot-check on a random 200 long answers from spec vs baseline to catch subtle factual omissions. I'll coordinate with QA.
Julia: will post results when job completes. TL;DR for now: great latency wins, measurable long-answer quality regressions that we should investigate before enabling spec by default on long-form tasks. :thinking_face:
